claims.text: The initial material is an as-cast equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr alloy.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a disordered BCC solid solution.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has excellent mechanical properties from room temperature through elevated temperatures near 1000 °C.
A portion of Hf should be replaced with Sc to form Hf1-xScxMoTaTiZr with x around 0.1–0.2.
The proposed alloys can be produced by arc melting followed by homogenization.
Hf-to-Sc substitution at the proposed level will retain a disordered, predominantly single-phase BCC structure with minimal secondary-phase formation.
Retention of the single-phase BCC structure will maintain room-temperature and elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
Sc is much lighter than Hf.
Partial replacement of Hf by Sc will reduce the alloy's overall density.
Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr will continue to supply strong atomic interactions and solid-solution strengthening after Sc is introduced.
Mo supports higher room-temperature strength, while high-melting-point Mo and Ta support elevated-temperature strength in this refractory-alloy family.
The Sc-modified alloy will have lower density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The Sc-modified alloy will retain comparable yield strength at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C.
The Sc-modified alloy will retain comparable ductility at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C.
Limiting Sc substitution to approximately 20% of the Hf sublattice will preserve BCC stability and prevent degradation of mechanical properties through approximately 1000 °C.
The applicable evaluation range is room temperature to approximately 1000 °C under tensile or compressive loading relevant to structural applications.
A greater than 10–15% loss in yield strength or ductility relative to the x=0 control is specified as a falsifying outcome.
Observation of secondary phases that compromise the single-phase BCC structure at room temperature or approximately 1000 °C is specified as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is restricted to roughly x=0.1–0.2 and the boundary recommends no more than about 20% Hf-site replacement, but the experiment extends to x=0.25 and states that failure at any substitution level falsifies the whole hypothesis. Failure only at x=0.25 would be outside the stated applicability boundary and should not reject successful compositions within it.

The mediator permits minimal secondary-phase formation, whereas the rejection language can be read as rejecting the hypothesis when secondary phases are observed. The rule partly qualifies this as phases that compromise the BCC structure, but no quantitative allowable phase fraction is given.
